item: Early CLI death hint — 'Your Claude CLI may be out of date' on a pre-stream exit (2026-09-05)
branch: a non-zero __exit frame carrying early:true (the process died before routing a single stream-json frame) renders a muted hint line under the stderr box; a mid-session crash (early absent) renders exactly what it does today — no hint
provenance: __exit is OUR OWN host frame, built in ChatPanel.onExit — it never rides the CLI wire, so this fixture is renderer-vs-frame self-consistency by construction. The `early` flag is set Kotlin-side when ClaudeCli.route() saw no parseable stdout frame before waitFor() returned; that half is NOT covered here and is live-verified separately (a stub `claude` on PATH printing a commander error and exiting 1 → hint present; SIGKILL of a real mid-idle CLI → hint absent). The SYMPTOM is real: a friend's fresh install (screenshot 2026-09-04) ran a pre-2.1.220 CLI that rejects `--permission-mode manual` → exit 1, and the panel showed only the raw crash. The stderr text in half A is copied verbatim from that screenshot. Decision 2026-09-05: no vocab translation, no version floor — a hint only (update button deferred).

steps.note: half A: early death → red exit line + ERR box + ONE muted hint under the box; half B (negative control): same exit without `early` → no hint
steps.setup: window.__ex73 = (function () { window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__clear'})); window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__exit', code:1, early:true, stderr:"error: option '--permission-mode <mode>' argument 'manual' is invalid. Allowed choices are acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, default, dontAsk, plan."})); const a = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('#log .status')); const exitA = a.filter(function (l) { return l.textContent.indexOf('claude process exited (1)') !== -1; }); const hintA = a.filter(function (l) { return l.textContent.indexOf('may be out of date') !== -1; }); const boxA = document.querySelectorAll('#log .io').length; const hintAfterBox = hintA.length === 1 && !!hintA[0].previousElementSibling && hintA[0].previousElementSibling.className === 'io'; window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__clear'})); window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__exit', code:1, stderr:'JavaScript heap out of memory'})); const b = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('#log .status')); const hintB = b.filter(function (l) { return l.textContent.indexOf('may be out of date') !== -1; }); const exitB = b.filter(function (l) { return l.textContent.indexOf('claude process exited (1)') !== -1; }); return { exitRedA: exitA.length === 1 && exitA[0].classList.contains('err'), hintCount: hintA.length, hintMuted: hintA.length === 1 && !hintA[0].classList.contains('err'), hintAfterBox: hintAfterBox, errBoxA: boxA, hintB: hintB.length, exitB: exitB.length }; })();

expect.why: DISCRIMINATING: the early exit renders exactly one 'may be out of date' hint line (pre-fix: 0)
DISCRIMINATING: the hint wears the plain muted status dress, not .err — it is advice, not a second error
GUARD: the hint sits directly under the stderr .io box, not above the crash it explains
GUARD: the existing red 'claude process exited (1)' line is untouched
GUARD: the folded ERR stderr box still renders alongside the hint
GUARD (negative control): a mid-session crash — `early` absent — gets no out-of-date hint
GUARD: the control half actually rendered its exit line (proves half B ran, not vacuous)
